links.outcome: Readability (FRES, FKGL) of LLM-generated CHF patient education texts
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 lowest readability (FRES 19.32, FKGL 14.28); ERNIEBot and Qwen most readable (FRES ≈ 59; FKGL ≈ 8), still above typical patient reading levels for some platforms.
links.quote: DeepSeek-R1 showed the greatest information completeness [EQIP-36 39.20 (36.17-44.23); χ2 = 25.07, P < 0.001] but the lowest readability [FRES 19.32 (17.94-36.89) and FKGL 14.28 (13.02-15.85); both P < 0.001].

links.outcome: Plain-language comprehensibility and actionability of LLM patient education outputs
links.effect: Overall quality high (GQS median 5.00), but readability varied widely across platforms and PEMAT-P actionability was limited overall at 20.00% (0.00-40.00).
links.quote: Actionability was limited overall [PEMAT-P actionability 20.00% (0.00-40.00); χ2 = 26.40, P < 0.001] and varied by topic, with daily management and prevention outperforming disease knowledge and diagnosis/classification (χ2 = 20.86, P < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Enhanced retrieval and structured template generation to improve LLM patient education texts
Comparing LLM platforms on PEMAT-P/EQIP/GQS for platform selection

screen.reason: The study evaluates responses generated by five LLMs to 20 CHF patient-education questions assessing quality, readability, and actionability, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
